issue.title: Require Closes #NNN only on PRs targeting main (stacked-PR tracker guardrail)
issue.body:
### Problem statement

GitHub only auto-closes issues when a PR with `Closes #NNN` / `Fixes #NNN` merges into the **default branch**. Stacked PRs that merge into a feature branch (base ≠ `main`) leave issues open even when the code later lands on `main` via a later squash.

This caused tracker drift during the 2026-07 audit:

- #105 stayed open after PR #251 (`Closes #105`) because base was `mrace/feature/103-harden-user-projects-fk`, not `main`. Code reached `main` via #248.
- #233 stayed open after PR #254 (`Closes #233`) because base was `mrace/feature/176-review-scrub-seekable`. Remux is still only on that stack / PR #252 until it merges to `main`.

### Scope

- Update delivery / issue-tracking docs (and optionally `.cursor/rules/delivery.mdc`) so agents and humans:
  - Prefer `Closes #NNN` **only** when the PR base is `main` and the PR completes the issue.
  - On stacked PRs, use `Part of #NNN` (no closing keyword) and close the issue from the final-to-`main` PR (or manually after merge).
- Optionally add a short checklist item to the PR template Reviewer checklist.

### Out of scope

- Changing GitHub org rules / required status checks (unless a cheap Actions check is agreed later).
- Rewriting historical stacked PR history.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/issue-tracking.md` documents the stacked-PR closing rule with the #105/#233 examples (or equivalent).
- [ ] Delivery rules / PR template point authors at the same rule.
- [ ] New developer / agent onboarding references the rule in one sentence.

### Verification

- [ ] Docs reviewed against a hypothetical stacked PR (base ≠ main) — would not claim auto-close.
- [ ] No code behavior change required.

### Priority

P1 — prevents recurring Project 4 / Issues drift.

### Links

- https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue
- Audit close comments on #105 / #233
